title: 1966 AHSME Problem 33
statement:
If \(ab\ne0\) and \(|a|\ne|b|,\) the number of distinct values of \(x\) satisfying the equation

\[ \begin{aligned} \frac{x-a}{b}+\frac{x-b}{a} &=\frac{b}{x-a}\\ &\quad+\frac{a}{x-b} \end{aligned} \]

is:

solutions.text:
Let \(N=(a+b)x-a^2-b^2.\) Combining each side gives \[ N\left(\frac1{ab} -\frac1{(x-a)(x-b)}\right)=0. \] The first factor gives \(x=\frac{a^2+b^2}{a+b}.\) The second gives \((x-a)(x-b)=ab,\) or \(x(x-a-b)=0,\) giving \(x=0\) and \(x=a+b.\) The hypotheses ensure that all three are defined and distinct.

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Both sides contain the numerator \((a+b)x-(a^2+b^2)\) after combining terms
Factor the equation into that numerator times a difference of reciprocals
